python.card-stranded/no-run: 🚨 stranded-watchdog: no agent run has started. Observed: this card has sat in Todo for 30+ minutes with no run receipt on it — every agent posts one the moment it starts, so as far as this sweep can see, nothing has begun. Why it has not started is not known from here, so this card needs a human to look. Evidence: last dispatch: none on record; run lookup: agent-task.yml lists no run for this card in the last 45 minutes (0 run(s) checked). To re-send it, run `linear_ops.py unpark DRE-1`, which clears the hold for you, or remove the 'needs-human' label and move the card out of Todo and back. Once the hygiene agent's holds lane is live (DRE-6172), a re-send needs no clearing: the hold lifts itself on the first run receipt newer than its stamp.

python.work-never-landed/branch:
🚨 unlanded-work-watchdog branch agent/DRE-1-slug: the branch `agent/DRE-1-slug` carries 3 commit(s) that are not on `main`, and no pull request has ever been opened for it — so nothing in the pipeline can see this work. CI, the critic, the merge gate and the Linear sync all key off a pull request; a branch on its own passes through no gate at all and closes no card. Last commit 240 minutes ago.

Where it goes from here: open a pull request from `agent/DRE-1-slug` into `main`. Hand-built work lands exactly the way dispatched work does — the branch, then the pull request, then the same checks and the same critic verdict. What changes is who writes the code, never how it lands.

_Posted once per branch. Opening the pull request ends it._
python.work-never-landed/no-branch:
🚨 unlanded-work-watchdog no branch: this card has sat in Todo for 240 minutes with nothing to point at: no branch, no pull request. It is labelled 'hand-built', so no dispatched run is coming by design — which also means the stranded-card watchdog stays silent on it (DRE-2524). This notice is what stands in its place.

What is missing, in order: a branch named `agent/DRE-1-<slug>`, then a pull request from it. Hand-built work meets the same checks and the same critic verdict as dispatched work — the only difference is who writes the code. If the work is deliberately paused, say so on the card, so the pause is a decision rather than a silence.

_Posted once per card._

python.merge-ref-refreshed:
stale-merge-ref-refresh @f00dfacef00dfacef00dfacef00dfacef00dface

Pull request #7 was red on 1 check(s) that were red on its merge base (`0badc0de`) too, and are green on `main` at `f00dface`:

- **Console backend (pytest)** — red on `d34db33f` and on the merge base, green on `main`.

`main` carried the fix in `f00dface`, and this branch's CI had run against a merge ref computed before it. Re-running the same jobs would re-run them against the same merge commit, so we refreshed the merge ref: the fault was on main, not in this pull request. The branch was refreshed with `update-branch` once for this `main` commit (1/3 refreshes used on this pull request).

What it costs, plainly: the new head is a merge of `main` into this branch. If the diff against `main` is unchanged, the standing critic verdict CARRIES (content binding, DRE-2340, `verdict_content.py`) and the critic skips the re-review. If `main`'s fix touched a file this branch also touches, the diff changed, the verdict is discharged and a fresh review runs.

python.reviewer-environment-hold:
🛑 runner-environment-hold @d34db33fcafe1234d34db33fcafe1234d34db33f: reviewer cannot run on this runner — native-binary-missing: the vendor action installed Claude Code but left no launcher on this runner, so nothing here can start Claude — twice on d34db33f; holding, nothing re-dispatched. Check: grep -n 'claude-code-action@' .github/workflows/*.yml in bureau-pipeline, then compare the pinned SHA with anthropics/claude-code-action#1817 (DRE-3416 pinned v1.0.217; DRE-3417 moved it to v1.0.234 / Claude Code 2.1.282 on 2026-09-25; DRE-5116 moved it to v1.0.236 / Claude Code 2.1.284 on 2026-09-28).

What failed is the runner's environment, not the work: no verdict was written, nothing in this pull request was rejected, and nothing has been re-dispatched.

**How this is released:** the first critic verdict posted in this repository after this hold, or a comment on the held pull request whose whole body is `▶️ re-run the review`, re-dispatches the held review once. Until one of those happens, nothing else is coming.
python.reviewer-outage-fleet-wide:
🚨 fleet-reviewer-outage @2026-09-08T22:19:00Z: the code reviewer is down across the fleet — 3 runs in 1 repos could not run since 15:19 PT, and none of them reached a verdict. Reviewer down since 15:19 PT — 3 runs, 1 repos.

What this is NOT: nothing in any of those pull requests was rejected and no work has been judged. The pipeline has stopped re-dispatching reviews into a reviewer that cannot start, and handed this to a person.

The card names the first failed run, the exact error line, the action reference those runs used and the three checks that tell the causes apart. The sweep closes it on the first successful verdict it can see in a repository it counted, after that repository's last counted crash.

Nothing is broken and nothing is retrying: this pull request needs a person to take it from here. Said once per commit; a new commit says it again.
